title: Options
headline: Option A — bounded buffer with early rejection — is the only shape whose failure mode reaches the producer.
synthesis:
## Options: how the ingest queue should shed load

Three approaches were drafted independently and judged against the same brief: keep p99 admission latency under 200ms when the upstream producer bursts to ten times its steady rate, without dropping an event the producer believes it delivered.

### The options as drafted

| Option | Shape | What it costs |
|---|---|---|
| **A — Bounded buffer, reject early** | A fixed in-memory ring in front of the writer. When the ring is full the admission handler returns 429 with a retry hint, so the producer keeps the event and retries it. | The producer must implement retry with backoff. Nothing else changes, and the failure mode is one the producer already handles for network errors. |
| **B — Spill to disk** | Overflow is written to a local segment file and drained when the writer catches up. Admission never fails while disk remains. | A second durability story: segments must be fsynced, replayed on restart, and garbage collected. Disk-full becomes a new failure mode with no back-pressure signal. |
| **C — Shed by priority** | Events carry a class; under pressure the low class is dropped and the high class is admitted. | Requires the producer to classify every event correctly, and the classification becomes a contract the receiver cannot verify. Silent loss is invisible to the producer. |

### Why A

Option A is the only one whose failure mode the producer can observe. B moves the problem rather than solving it — the queue still has a bound, it is just the disk, and reaching it is now silent and unrecoverable. C makes correctness depend on a classification the receiving side cannot check, which turns a load problem into a data-integrity problem.

A's cost is real: the producer needs retry with backoff. That work is bounded, it is the producer's own code, and it makes back-pressure explicit rather than hiding it behind a buffer that will eventually fill anyway.

### What this does not settle

- The ring's size is left open. It should be derived from the measured drain rate rather than guessed.
- If a future producer cannot retry, B becomes worth revisiting for that path alone — not for the default.
limits: No load test was run; the 200ms target is unverified against any of the three shapes.
The ring size is left open and should be derived from a measured drain rate.

fields.name: winner
fields.value: A — bounded buffer with early rejection

fields.name: rationale
fields.value: A is the only option whose failure mode reaches the producer. B replaces a bounded queue with a larger bounded queue and adds a silent, unrecoverable failure at the new bound; C makes correctness depend on a classification the receiver cannot verify. A's cost — retry with backoff at the producer — is bounded, local, and already implemented for network errors.

claims.statement: Option B does not remove the bound, it moves it to the disk, where exhaustion produces no back-pressure signal and cannot be recovered without operator action.
Option C's priority classification is set by the producer and cannot be validated by the consumer, so a misclassification presents as silent data loss rather than as an error.
The producer already implements retry with exponential backoff for transport errors, so option A's added cost is a status-code branch rather than new machinery.

summary: Three approaches to shedding load on the ingest queue were drafted independently and judged against one brief. Option A — a bounded buffer that rejects early — is the only shape whose failure mode reaches the producer, and it is recommended. findings.title: Bounded buffer that rejects early
findings.impact: The only shape whose failure mode reaches the producer: a full ring returns 429 and the producer keeps the event.
findings.action: Adopt. The producer already retries transport errors, so the added cost is a status-code branch.

findings.title: Spill overflow to disk
findings.impact: Moves the bound to the disk rather than removing it, and exhaustion there is silent and unrecoverable without an operator.
findings.action: Revisit only for a future producer that cannot retry, never as the default.

findings.title: Shed by producer-declared priority
findings.impact: Correctness would depend on a classification the receiver cannot verify, turning a load problem into silent data loss.

ask.do: Approve the bounded buffer so the build can start.
ask.why: It is the only design where a full buffer tells the sender to retry instead of losing events.
